These revisions have been filed by the husband, who is facing proceedings in DVA.No.86 of 2023 (CRP.No.2414 of 2023) and by the parents- in-law of the respondent in the very same DVA proceedings (CRP.No.2418 of 2023), pending on the file of the Special Court to try cases under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence, Coimbatore.

sentences.text: The said domestic violence complaint has been initiated by the respondent, wife of the petitioner in CRP.No.2414 of 2023 and daughter-in-law of the petitioners in CRP.No.2418 of 2023.
2.I have heard Mr.V.Raghavachari, learned Senior Counsel for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(
Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm ) CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023 Mr.N.C.Ashok Kumar,
learned counsel for the petitioner in CRP.No.2414 of 2023, Mr.N.C.Ashok Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners in CRP.No.2418 of 2023 and Mr.A.K.Sriram, learned Senior Counsel for Mr.A.Selvendran, learned counsel for the 1st respondent in both CRPs.

3.Mr.V.Raghavachari, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner would state that the 1st respondent and the petitioner in CRP.No.2414 of 2023 are husband and wife and the husband has already initiated proceedings for divorce and there is also an order for payment of interim maintenance,
which is being promptly paid to meet the expenses of the minor child. According to the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, the domestic violence proceedings were initiated after the filing of the HMOP and clearly amounts to a counter blast to the said proceedings.

The learned Senior Counsel would state that there is also a guardian OP that has been filed by the petitioner and both the HMOP and the GWOP were filed in March 2023 and after receiving summons in these proceedings, the respondent has proceeded to file domestic violence complaint on 18.05.2023, at Coimbatore.

2 4.The

learned Senior Counsel, Mr.V.Raghavachari, would further state that the allegations of illicit relationship between the 1st respondent and strangers have been made in the HMOP and photographs were also relied on by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm ) CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023 the learned Senior Counsel to fortify his contention that the 1st respondent's character is not of good moral standing.

He would further state that the petitioner is from a very reputed family and are well known in the business circles as well and without any basis and prior complaint, the respondent has chosen to file a domestic violence complaint, blowing hot and cold, only in order to bring down the reputation of the petitioner family.

He would invite my attention to the documents that were filed along with the domestic violence complaint and contend that not even a prima facie case has been made out for the domestic violence complaint being even taken on file.

5.Mr.N.C.Ashok Kumar, the learned counsel for the petitioners in CRP.No.2418 of 2023 would state that the matrimonial home is far away from the residence of the parents-in-law, who stayed at Madurai and he would also adopt the submissions made by the learned Senior Counsel,
Mr.V.Raghavachari.

He would also take me through the order passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court, which was in respect of the guardian OP proceedings, where the Hon'ble Division Bench has held that the respondent has filed applications for interim maintenance, only to feed her ego and is attempting to misuse judicial process for such purpose.
The learned counsel would point out that the appeals filed by the respondent were dismissed with costs of Rs.50,000/- in each of the Civil Miscellaneous Appeals.

In short, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm ) CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023 contention of the petitioners, namely the husband as well as the in-laws, is that the domestic violence complaint is only an after thought and counter blast to the HMOP proceedings, where serious allegations have been made against the 1st respondent and there is absolutely no cause of action for filing the domestic violence complaint,
especially against the in-laws, who reside in Madurai and the parties do not reside under the same roof.
6.It is also the contention of Mr.N.C.Ashok Kumar that no details, with specific dates have been provided in the complaint, warranting the Magistrate to take cognizance of such vague and generic allegations.
In this backdrop, the petitioners seek for the domestic violence complaint to be struck off.
He would therefore pray for the revisions being allowed.

7.Per contra, Mr.A.K.Sriram, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the 1st respondent, would invite my attention to the grounds of challenge in both the revisions and state that all grounds related to factual matrix and not even a single ground alleging a patent lack of jurisdiction has been raised.

Therefore, he would state that, as held by the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Arul Danial and Others Vs. Suganya, reported in (2022) 3 MWN (Crl) 539, there is no grounds to interfere under Article 227 of Constitution of India, that too, in order to strike off the domestic violence complaint.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Senior Counsel https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm ) CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023 would further state that even if the domestic violence complaint is alleged to be a counter blast to the divorce proceedings initiated by the husband, it would be irrelevant for deciding the domestic violence complaint, the considerations of which are totally on a different platform altogether.

He would also state that there is absolutely no limitation for filing a Ashwanth Pothy vs Asmitha Alanknitha on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85522362/
3 domestic violence complaint and the observations that have been made by the Hon'ble Division Bench in maintenance proceedings are also not relevant and would not have a bearing insofar as the domestic violence complaint is concerned, which is entirely on a different and an independent cause of action.
He would invite my attention to the domestic violence complaint itself and would emphasis on the various kinds of abuses that have been alleged by the respondent against all these petitioners.
He would therefore state that there is absolutely no ground for striking off the domestic violence complaint as prayed by the petitioners.
8.I have carefully considered the submissions advanced by the learned counsel and learned Senior Counsel on either side.

9.It is now settled law that in order to initiate a complaint under the DV Act, there is no period of limitation and therefore, to allege that the complaint is belated and therefore is liable to be strike off is of no avail. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm )
CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023
10.With regard to the allegations that have been made against the petitioners
, I find that the respondent has cited several incidents of abuse against all the petitioners.
These are factual matters that can be decided only by the Magistrate, after the parties lead oral and documentary evidence.

As held by the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Arul Danial's case, unless there is patent lack of jurisdiction shown, this Court should not interfere under Article 227 of Constitution of India and strike off the complaint.

11.As rightly pointed by Mr.A.K.Sriram, learned Senior Counsel for the respondent, even in the grounds raised in the revisions, they are all relating to only the factual matrix and not a single ground challenges or attacks the lack of jurisdiction of the Magistrate to take the complaint on file.

The legal contention that was argued by Mr.V.Raghavachari, learned Senior Counsel is that the Magistrate should apply his mind before entertaining the complaint and in the present case there was absolutely no application of mind by the Magistrate and therefore, the complaint is a gross abuse, which should be nipped in the bud.

The learned counsel for the petitioners have relied on the following decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court:
1.Achin Gupta Vs. State of Haryana and Another ((2025) 3 SCC 756).

sentences.text: 12.The learned Senior Counsel for the respondent would rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Arul Danial's case and refer to the various directions and guidelines that have been issued in the concluding portions of the said judgment.

13.Insofar as the decision in Shaurabh Kumar Tripathi's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was only addressing the issue whether Section 482 of Cr.P.C and now Section 528 of BNSS, 2023, can be invoked to quash the proceedings initiate under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from the Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

entities.text: Protection of Women from the Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has ultimately held that a petition under Section 482 now Section 528 of BNSS, 2023, emanating from Section 12(1) of the DV Act is maintainable and further held that interference would be warranted only in the case of gross illegality or injustice.

14.In Achin Gupta's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that Court should be mindful of adverse consequences of filing false complaints of cruelty against the husband and relatives and many times,
a mountain out of a molehill is made and out of sheer hatred, the husband and all his family members are harassed by lodging complaints.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Dr.P.Pathmanathan's case

, this Court held that the complaint under Section 498A of IPC was a counter blast to the divorce petition filed by the 1 st accused in the facts of the said case and it amounted to a clear abuse of process of law and the proceedings in the criminal case were quashed.

However, in the facts of those case, this Court gave weightage to the report submitted by the Deputy Superintendent of Police, stating that there is no dowry harassment and it was only a case of misunderstanding between the husband and the wife, which led to separation and divorce proceedings being initiated.
In such circumstances, this Court proceeded to quash the complaint.

16.In Kailashben Mahendrbhal's case, the Honble Supreme Court held that on the facts of the said case, it was seen that proceedings were instituted with malafide intention to harass the appellants by filing the domestic violence complaint.
However, in the said case, the domestic violence complaint went to trial and culminated in a detailed judgment and appeal proceedings were also resorted to.
In such circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the ingredients of Section 498A was not made out and a criminal proceedings were an abuse of process of law.

Even while holding that the High Court can take cognizance on the criminal side, as held in Shaurabh Kumar Tripathi's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has clearly cautioned the High Courts that exercise of interference cannot be in a routine manner, but only where there is a case of gross illegality and injustice.
18.In such view of the matter

, examining the domestic violence complaint and the grounds seeking striking off the same, I am unable to find any such challenge to the complaint on the ground of the Ashwanth Pothy vs Asmitha Alanknitha on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85522362/
5 same being grossly illegal or unjust.

sentences.text: Moreover, as already discussed, there is no ground of challenge regarding any patent lack of jurisdiction to entertain the domestic violence complaint.
19.The only argument that deserves consideration is the Magistrate taking cognizance of the complaint, without any application of mind.

As held by the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court in Arul Danial's case, even in such cases, interference under Article 227 of Constitution of India is not desirable and a remedy available is even under the statute to go back to the Magistrate and seek for modification of the orders.

Therefore, unless the petitioners are able to show that there is an inherent and patent lack of jurisdiction for entertaining the complaint itself or gross injustice caused, then alone this Court can interfere and strike off the domestic violence complaint.
No such grounds have been made https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 08/08/2025 05:43:13 pm ) CRP.Nos.2414 & 2418 of 2023 out in the present case warranting such interference.
All the grounds that are raised are revolving around contentious and factual matters, which can be effectively adjudicated only upon the parties leading oral and documentary evidence.

Therefore I do not find any case made out for striking off the domestic violence complaint at the instance of the petitioners, invoking under Article 227 of Constitution of India.
20.However, as held by the Hon'ble Full Bench of this Court, the physical presence of the petitioners may not be insisted ordinarily by the Magistrate and only when it is absolutely necessary, for their examination in chief and cross alone.
21.In fine
, the Civil Revision Petitions are dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Connected Civil Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
